Kench, Jones, Garland and Ford, were third in the final of the Under 19 Relay, beaten by Herne Hill H. and Polytechnic H.; and R.

A team consisting of Tosh, Scrimshaw, Williams (J.S.), Powter, Gratte, Clemens, Kench, and Ford (A.J.) made up the club team. The start from Baker Street was not at all encouraging, as the rain was descending in torrents, accompanied by plenty of lightning and thunder.
Our 'bus left Westminster shortly after 10-30 a.m. and we made for Clapham Common, where Jack Flower, our first man, would hand on to Alfred Kench.
Sixteen men lined up at the start, and it was thought before hand that it would be a race between Penny, Rice and Kench, but I believe the last-named was really the favourite.

Scrimshaw, Tosh, Clemens, Holder, Allum, Michael, Ford, Kench, Tame, Basford and Jarvis all performed creditably in the highest class without being able to claim one of the first four places which alone carry points to the Club's credit.
The 1 Mile match resulted in an easy win for Tommy Hampson, who is also a member of our own Club, but Kench ran a good race in a plucky endeavour to hang on.
Kench and J.

In the 4 x 880 yards we scored an easy win in slow time, Alf Kench running a fine half to give us a good lead which was kept to the finish. The 4 x 300 again saw us placed third, only this time Croydon beat Mitcham.
Our team was Michael, Tosh (who took us into the lead), Kench and Scrimshaw; the time of 8 min. 9 secs was good, considering the bad weather conditions.
Basford led off well for us by capturing the sprint; and later Kench, our mile champion, surprised everyone by his excellent running in the 440 yards event, which he won in fast time.
Pack, accounted for the 440 yards, Kench just failing to give him five yards. Those who enjoy picking out coming champions should not have to look much further than the results which are appended.
For us Morgan (100 yards), Tosh (880 yards) and Kench (440 yards) were winners. All the events were keenly contested and we look forward to a renewal of this fixture next year.

The next championship to change hands was the half-mile A change was inevitable since Tom Scrimshaw, the holder, was away, and in the absence of Jim Tosh, who was busy elsewhere getting married, Kench was left as favourite.

Williams is a young schoolmaster resident in London, and we have every hope that he will prove an addition to our cross-country strength. Kealey could not be caught by Kench in the 440 yards final, whilst the 100 yards handicap was taken by J.
Kealey, but Kealey had his reward for some consistent sprinting throughout the season in winning the 220 yards title. Alf Kench retained his 440 yards championship in a close finish with R.

In the 4 x 100 yards we had Kench running a leg for us and we did as expected in finishing third behind Croydon and Mitcham. The 4 x 880 yards saw Michael going off first of our lads and he ran finely in setting up a lead over the other clubs.
Michael, Kench and Shields have served the Club well, and Stimpson and Ball shown promise. Of the milers, Rice, Shaw and Jordan have done well.
